rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest candidate: chunk 5 line 87 "If the picked path only loads when named, ask for the `@import` line before you move on." — "the picked path" is not a verbatim earlier noun, but chunk 4 ("Decide the location with Claude") is the immediately preceding chunk naming the same act; this is immediate continuation of the prior slide's subject, an explicit non-violation per the rule's own carve-out ("one more window"-type continuation), not a stray referent.

chunk 3 line 35: "The same move you ran at M1 on a bug ticket, pointed at a story." — named by module code (M1), not located by position ("the previous module"); verified close-the-ticket.md (M1's exercise) does read a bug ticket (## Read the ticket for your bug, line 11), so the name resolves to a real, correctly-described artifact. Line 88's link to claude-code-for-engineers.md is named by title, not positioned on a page.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 3 lines 35-36: "the same move you ran at M1" / "the bug fields" — verified against curriculum/exercises/close-the-ticket.md, which currently carries '## Read the ticket for your bug' and '## Read the conventions off the ticket' (bug-ticket-conventions read). The referenced beat exists and matches the description; this is also the exact split the maintainer block documents (2026-08-12 rename note, line 122 of expanded view).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-then-reveal construction anywhere in the body; the file has no live-demo beat for this rule to apply to.

closest candidate: chunk 2 (lines 29-32), the shortest chunk, one bullet only — "The rule that arrives generic... is the one to rewrite in your words, or reject." This is a self-carrying instruction (a complete claim/directive), not a wait-state or context-dependent fragment, so it stands on its own as a slide.

closest candidate: chunk 5 header "Where rules can live, and when they load" (line 75) against its content (a load-mechanism table, lines 77-83) — header states the table's exact content, no contradiction. All 7 headed chunks checked; each header is a literally true summary of its chunk's content.

Scanned body for each sub-item: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlatives (checked closest candidate, chunk 6 line 94 'Ask Claude what this file could drive later' — plain, not a value-prop claim); no number+retraction pattern; no abstraction-noun stacks; no empty-leg verb triplets. All sub-items PASS.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped body for surface/firing/compendium/forcing function/beat/mood/Connections — none present. Closest candidate: line 87 'ask for the @import line' and line 85 'facilitated by hooks and router skills' use ordinary Claude Code platform vocabulary (hooks, skills, @import), not repo-internal maintainer dialect — these are documented product terms, not authorial shorthand.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Bold instances in body: chunk 0 widget chrome ('**Time:**', '**What you do:**', '**What you build:**', '**The point:**', lines 3-9) — exempt per widget-chrome carve-out; '**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*' labels at lines 22, 41, 64, 96 — structural widget label pattern used identically across the corpus, not a narrative bold. No bolded bullet leads or whole-sentence bolding anywhere in body prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Verified via grep: this exercise is included by curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/plan-mode-done-right.md (a real training module file), the standard exercise-include mechanism that reaches the composed deck through the module's `.phase--exercise` wrapper. Not a phase-less orphan file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest candidate: chunk 5 header 'Where rules can live, and when they load' (line 75) — not literally imperative and not a phase label, but it is also not a declarative LAW-claim (the mood the rule targets); it is a topic label for a reference table, matching the same pattern as chunk 7's 'Read the shapes' family of non-Phase exercise headers elsewhere in the corpus. It does not create the imperative/declarative confusion the rule exists to prevent, so it stays inside the exercise-heading convention rather than crossing into lecture-claim territory.
